question: Combining pages 89 and 93 on Atlantification of the Arctic Ocean: at what depth ranges do the warm, salty Atlantic Water (AW) and the overlying Arctic halocline sit, how did halocline stratification change differently in the Amerasian Basin vs. the Eurasian Basin, and by what percentage did Eurasian Basin halocline stability decline over the preceding three decades?
ground_truth: Atlantic Water flows at 150–800 m depth, overlain by the Arctic halocline at ~50–150 m (and upper ~50 m fresh surface water). Stratification strengthened in the Amerasian Basin (slowing sea-ice loss) while weakening in the Eurasian Basin, where halocline stability declined by ~30% over the preceding three decades.

question: According to pages 120–121 on Rusting Rivers, beyond the 75 Brooks Range streams reported in 2024, more than how many discolored streams/rivers have been compiled in northern Alaska, how is the Landsat Redness Index calculated, and what Redness Index threshold distinguishes iron-discolored orange water from clear water?
ground_truth: More than 200 discolored streams and rivers have been compiled across >1000 km; Redness Index is calculated as the ratio of surface reflectance of the red and blue bands; values > 1.5 (orange circles) indicate iron-discolored water whereas < 1.5 (grey circles) indicate clear water.
